Compa SA Unveils New Precision Components Line, Eyes Export Growth

Romania-based automotive supplier Compa SA announced the launch of a new line of advanced precision components on Thursday, as the company seeks to bolster its position in the European automotive supply chain and expand its export footprint.

The new product range, which includes machined turbocharger housings and high-tolerance gear assemblies, is designed to serve next-generation passenger and commercial vehicles, according to company officials. Production has commenced at Compa SA’s Sibiu manufacturing facility, a site that has seen steady investment in automation and quality control technologies in recent years.

“Today’s launch marks an important step in Compa SA’s strategy to become a partner of choice for global automotive manufacturers,” said Monica Dumitru, Chief Commercial Officer at Compa SA. “Our new product line leverages both the technical expertise of our team and the competitive advantages of Romania’s industrial sector.”

The company expects the new line to contribute up to €18 million annually in additional revenues once full-scale production is reached, projected for late 2025. Compa SA reported total revenues of €184 million in 2023, with nearly 70% generated from exports to Western and Central Europe. The precision components are aimed at both existing clients and new customers in markets including Germany, France, and the Czech Republic.

Mircea Popescu, an automotive sector analyst at FinVest Solutions, noted that Compa SA’s expansion comes amid robust demand for lightweight and energy-efficient components, as manufacturers adapt to stricter emissions regulations and electrification trends. “Compa SA is well-placed to benefit from these shifts,” Popescu said. “Their focus on precision manufacturing aligns with the evolving requirements of their OEM clients.”

Industry observers point to Compa SA’s ongoing investments in workforce development and digitalization as key factors supporting the company’s growth. The company employs over 1,800 staff in Sibiu, a city known for its automotive engineering talent pool. “We have partnered with technical universities and vocational schools to ensure a steady pipeline of skilled labor,” Dumitru added.

The Romanian Association of Automotive Suppliers welcomed the launch, highlighting the role of local companies in strengthening the country’s export profile. “Romania’s automotive industry has demonstrated resilience and adaptability,” said Radu Marinescu, the association’s president. “Initiatives like this one from Compa SA showcase our sector’s capacity for innovation.”

Compa SA plans to present the new product line at the upcoming EuroTech Auto Expo in Bucharest next month. The company is also exploring potential collaborations with electric vehicle startups and commercial fleet manufacturers.

Shares in Compa SA rose 1.2% on the Bucharest Stock Exchange following the announcement.
